text: In February 2017 our language collected around one occasion. At our peak on February 28, eighty-seven of us said "joint session of congress," seventy-one "a joint session," seventy "a joint session of congress," sixty-three "to a joint session of congress," forty-eight "address to a joint session of," and thirty-seven "address to congress." That phrasing did not begin with us; it first entered the record on January 25, 2013, from Tim Walberg. Earlier in the month our attention divided: forty-one of us said "national security advisor" on February 14, thirty-nine "secretary of education" on February 7. We did not add to these words. We restated the occasion in fragments, and the counts are what we left behind.
